rationale: Cardholder C08106 disputes the $128.33 online charge 3583227 (2016-12-29), which is 3.63x their 180-day mean of $35.31 (z=3.36) on a card whose history is entirely online/product C with an average basket around $35. The transaction came from a device never seen on this card ('unknown | unknown | firefox 47.0 | unknown', flagged New for the account) and a different email domain (hotmail) than the prior-day $92.86 charge (gmail), which is itself 2.63x mean and also carries a New device flag - a two-transaction burst in under 24h that matches card-not-present fraud from a new device. Memory on this exact card is split but informative: CC-3778 on C08106-K1 was a confirmed CNP fraud of the same shape (single unrecognized online purchase, inconsistent amount), while CC-0696 on the same card was cleared after the cardholder confirmed travel - so a dispute here is not automatically fraud, but the earlier confirmed compromise raises the prior. The rare-device links in the graph rest on generic strings (Windows/chrome/edge shared by dozens of cards); the flagged device profile itself appears on only 6 cards all-time and just 1 in this window, so I do not treat this as a ring case. Taken together - explicit denial, new device, 3.4-sigma amount, a second same-shape charge the day before, and a prior confirmed CNP fraud on this card - the evidence supports fraud without needing a further request.
